title: MergeShuffle: Reconstruct Shared Libraries for Improved Performance and Security
abstract: arXiv:2610.22952v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Debloating shared libraries has been an active research topic for years. Tools for shared library debloating rely on either static or dynamic analysis techniques to discover which parts of the shared library is used. Once these parts are found, these tools take one of two routes, either removing parts of the library that are not used, requiring reconstruction of the library; or they simply overwriting the unused functions. However, recently a broad study~\cite{brown2024broad} on debloating tools has shown that some of these tools either increase the static binary size, or are generally less effective for complex workloads.   In this paper, we argue that shared-library debloaters' performance can be improved by proper reconstruction of the shared-libraries once the used functions in the library are identifies. We propose \myapp, a novel tool for reconstructing shared libraries from a given set of file ranges to eliminate unused code based

translated_title: MergeShuffle：重构共享库以提升性能与安全性
translated_abstract: 共享库瘦身多年来一直是一个活跃的研究课题。共享库瘦身工具依赖静态或动态分析技术来发现共享库中哪些部分被使用。一旦找到这些部分，这些工具会采取两种路径之一：要么移除库中未使用的部分（这需要对库进行重构），要么直接覆写未使用的函数。然而，最近一项针对瘦身工具的广泛研究表明，其中一些工具要么会增加静态二进制文件的大小，要么在处理复杂工作负载时总体效果较差。在本文中，我们认为一旦识别出共享库中被使用的函数，通过对共享库进行恰当的重构，可以提升共享库瘦身工具的性能。我们提出了MergeShuffle，一种新颖的工具，可以根据给定的文件范围集合来重构共享库，从而消除未使用的代码。
tldr: 本文提出MergeShuffle工具，通过在识别出共享库中被使用的函数后对其进行恰当重构以消除未使用代码，从而提升共享库瘦身在性能与安全性方面的效果。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes MergeShuffle, a novel tool that reconstructs shared libraries from given file ranges to eliminate unused code, improving the performance and security of shared-library debloating.
